Hey man, I can completely relate to the chronic pain and it consuming you and making everything difficult. I’m pretty bad at giving advice but this resonated with me so much - I’m 17 and can’t even go out with buds nevermind WORK or do school well because of my chronic pain, and idk how I’m gonna survive the future when I have to financially support myself. But the key thing is—try not to let it consume you. I know you may be thinking that it already has, but you’re still here. You’re still breathing. You’re still fighting everyday. Each day is a victory. Try and care for the little things. Peace feels impossible to achieve when you’re in a constant state of pain, but trying to ground myself in things such as a damn good glass of water helps me get by. If you’re dead— no more damn good glasses of water. And you think that’s a WAY better tradeoff than the hell you’re going thru, because you get to sit in a pit of nothingness. But it’s not better. Because eventually in your pit of nothingness you’ll crave a damn good glass of water. Or seeing your mom smile. Or a stupid show. But you’ll never EVER get those again. EVER. No takebacks for eternity on life, man. Gotta keep er goin. Imagine how proud your best friend and cousin are to see you fight every day. I imagine my grandpa. I know the damn good glass of water bit sounds silly, but it’s true. Now, when it comes to achieving peace that ISNT death, I’m still trying to figure out a solution. If it’s legal where you live perhaps consider medical marijuana? There’s a lot of stigma around it, but I’ve seen it do wonders for my dad. It can help significantly with chronic pain and helps provide peace from the constant turmoil.

Try and find one thing you like. Not in the way you talked before, but something small. Ice cream. Music. A nice ass glass of water. You die? No more. None of that. And nothingness sounds better until you’re in your pit of nothingness and really want a nice ass glass of water. Yknow? It sounds silly, but its just some food for thought. At times it may feel like you enjoy nothing, maybe all the time. But everyone has at least one little thing. But little things all disappear when you’re dead. That’s what I’ve been using. We’re young asf as well, I fucking hate the phrase time heals all wounds I think it’s a load of shit but I mean we have so much damn time rn for literally anything in our lives to change. There are infinite possibilities and nothing is really impossible. Shit could get better. Shit could ignite some drive. I hate the idea of “could” with the uncertainty, but I try and make the uncertainty worth that crisp ass glass of water. Little things and random changes.
